\section[applaudire]{applaudire — to applaud}

\label{lesson:IT-C208-applaudire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to divorce, then the Italian for to move house.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: applaudire}
\textbf{applaudire} — \textquotedblleft{}to applaud\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{applaudire} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{applaudere}, \textquotedblleft{}to clap the hands\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ad}, \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{plaudere}, \textquotedblleft{}to clap\textquotedblright{} — a learned borrowing. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}
